note: ID replacement and transportation. Researched Oct 31 2026 for the matcher's gaps (no transport resources; legal aid offered for a lost state ID). Run the dry run and check each record before --commit.

resources.primary_services: Replaces a lost or stolen Michigan state ID or driver's license, and issues a new state ID. Visits by appointment at any branch office; some replacements online or at self-service stations.
resources.what_they_help_with: Replace a lost state ID or driver's license.
resources.description: The only office that issues a Michigan state ID. A duplicate can be ordered while the card is still unexpired; an expired card means applying for a new one, which needs proof of identity (birth certificate or passport), Social Security number and two proofs of Michigan residency.
resources.elig_notes: Standard ID replacement fee about $10 (waived at 65+ or legally blind) — confirm the current fee. Online replacement needs a valid Social Security card on file.
resources.what_to_bring: Old ID if they have it. For a new card: birth certificate or passport, Social Security card, two proofs of Michigan address (a shelter letter can count — ask the branch).

resources.parent: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
resources.primary_services: Certified copies of Michigan birth certificates — the document most often missing when someone needs a new state ID.
resources.what_they_help_with: Get a copy of a Michigan birth certificate.
resources.description: State vital records office. Orders online through VitalChek (the only authorized online vendor), by mail, or in person. County clerks in the county of birth also issue copies, often cheaper.
resources.eligibility_req: The person named on the record (or an eligible relative). Born in Michigan.
resources.elig_notes: State fee about $34 for a search and first copy; county clerks are often less. Free 'veterans benefits' copies exist but are stamped not for personal use, so they won't work for a state ID.
resources.phone_to_call: https://www.vitalchek.com — or the county clerk where they were born
resources.what_to_bring: Photo ID is usually required — if they have none, call first and ask what they accept.
resources.source: michigan.gov/mdhhs vital records pages — researched Oct 31 2026

resources.primary_services: Free copies of a veteran's DD-214 and other military service records, requested online (eVetRecs), by mail or by fax with Standard Form 180.
resources.what_they_help_with: Get a free copy of your DD-214.
resources.description: Holds the official military personnel files. Recently separated veterans can often download a DD-214 faster through DoD milConnect.
resources.eligibility_req: The veteran, or next of kin of a deceased veteran.
resources.elig_notes: Free to the veteran. Ask for the long form (member-4 copy) — it shows character of service, which benefit programs ask for.
resources.phone_to_call: https://www.archives.gov/veterans/military-service-records (eVetRecs) — or mail/fax SF-180 to NPRC, 1 Archives Drive, St. Louis, MO 63138
resources.what_to_bring: Full name used in service, Social Security number, branch, rough dates of service.

resources.primary_services: Free replacement Social Security card. Often needed to get a state ID, a job or a bank account.
resources.what_they_help_with: Replace a lost Social Security card, free.
resources.description: Free. Many people can request a replacement online with a my Social Security account; otherwise at a local Social Security office.
resources.eligibility_req: Anyone with a Social Security number.
resources.elig_notes: Usually needs proof of identity (state ID, or another accepted document if the ID is lost too) — call to ask what they'll accept.
resources.what_to_bring: Any ID they have. A VA health card or military ID can help.

resources.primary_services: Public buses and Link on-demand rides across Grand Traverse and Leelanau counties. Veterans ride at the reduced (half) fare.
resources.what_they_help_with: Buses and on-demand rides around Traverse City; half fare for veterans.
resources.description: Traverse City's public transit. Fixed-route buses in town, plus Link on-demand rides booked by phone, online or in the BATA Link app.
resources.eligibility_req: Open to everyone. Veterans and active military get reduced fare.
resources.elig_notes: Reduced fare: show a military/veteran ID or a BATA reduced-fare card (apply at a transfer station, bata.net, or info@bata.net). A bus pass is a good purchase to log against the veteran.
resources.phone_to_call: 231-941-2324 — or book Link rides in the BATA Link app
resources.what_to_bring: Veteran ID or BATA reduced-fare card for the half fare.
resources.source: bata.net; Traverse City Record-Eagle — researched Oct 31 2026

resources.primary_services: Free volunteer-driven rides to VA medical appointments, run through each VA medical center's DAV Hospital Service Coordinator.
resources.what_they_help_with: Free rides to VA medical appointments.
resources.description: Volunteer drivers in DAV vans. Booked locally through the VA medical center that serves the veteran, usually days ahead.
resources.eligibility_req: Veterans with a VA medical appointment and no other way to get there.
resources.elig_notes: Book through the local VA medical center's DAV coordinator, often 48 hours or more ahead. Riders must usually be able to walk without the driver's help. Can't also claim VA travel reimbursement for the same trip.
resources.phone_to_call: Call the veteran's VA medical center and ask for the DAV Hospital Service Coordinator
resources.source: va.gov DAV vans pages; dav.org — researched Oct 31 2026

resources.primary_services: Monthly discount on phone or internet service for people on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance or the VA Veterans Pension, or with low income.
resources.what_they_help_with: A cheap or free phone plan, so people can reach you.
resources.description: Federal program. Apply through the National Verifier, then sign up with a participating phone or internet company. Many carriers offer a free basic smartphone plan through it.
resources.eligibility_req: Low income, or on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, Federal Public Housing Assistance or the Veterans and Survivors Pension.
resources.elig_notes: One Lifeline benefit per household. A shelter address can work — ask the carrier.
resources.what_to_bring: Proof of SNAP, Medicaid, SSI or VA pension, or of income.
